rejectedBy: criterion 5 (coverage on the untouched final 5 confirmation origins): us-new-york cold_start reached 0.9620, above the 0.95 ceiling. OVER-coverage, not under-coverage -- the intervals became too wide. #85's band is symmetric for a reason: an over-wide P90 inflates safety stock exactly as an under-wide one starves it.
criterion 4 (confidence): mean cold-start confidence fell 46.9%, 0.5899 -> 0.3130, past the declared 33% limit taken from the C4 precedent.
criteriaThatDidPass: criterion 2: p50 byte-identical, so A1, WAPE, bias and every #77 display cell are unchanged by construction.
criterion 1 at the global and india-west level: cold_start 0.9178 all-origins and 0.9282 india-west confirmation both sit inside the band.
whyItFailed: The residual quantile is measured on development origins and applied to confirmation origins whose dispersion differs. Fitting the 90th percentile of residuals gave india-west a width that holds up and us-new-york one that overshoots, so a single conformal level per market x horizon does not transfer across time for this cohort. Combined with the 46.9% confidence loss, the reading is that honest cold-start dispersion at h12-h26 is simply very wide: calibrating to it produces an interval near twice p50, and the interval is then barely decision-useful even when its coverage is nominally correct.
conclusion: Two mechanisms in the post-hoc calibration class have now been rejected on preregistered criteria: C6 could not reach the target by rescaling a mis-shaped spread, and C7 reached it on average while breaching the band on held-out data and destroying nearly half the displayed confidence. Decision #87's own stop rule says a C7 failure authorises no third calibration attempt. The cold-start interval needs a MODELLED quantile head fitted on cold-start dispersion, not a correction applied to one fitted elsewhere -- which is a scope change with its own decision, not a variant of #87.
refusedRemedies: Relaxing the 0.95 ceiling to admit us-new-york's 0.9620. The band is symmetric because over-wide intervals over-stock; #85 already refused loosening the floor and the ceiling is the same principle.

Dropping criterion 4 after it bound. It is arguably mis-specified -- it can conflate width that buys calibration with width that buys nothing -- but C7 fails criterion 5 independently, so nothing turns on that argument and it is not used as a route to acceptance.
Refitting the conformal level on all 13 origins to make confirmation agree. That is fitting on the confirmation data, which is the one thing decision #74 exists to prevent.
